title: Same basename and roughly the same line, nothing else in common
why: ADVERSARIAL, and doubly so. Different directory, different enclosing symbol, different content, different pattern: only the basename and a nearby line coincide, which is exactly what a proximity heuristic latches onto. The second trap is the one this case originally fell into itself - having correctly refused the mapping, there is still no evidence that occ-a1 died or that occ-b1 was born, so BOTH sides are unresolved. Reporting ended plus new here is the proximity error committed twice: it turns 'I could not relate these' into a fix and a regression that never happened.

expect.note: Broker/Doc.cs is still present and was not observed to lose the site; nothing shows this occurrence ended
Reports/Doc.cs is not recorded as added, so nothing shows this occurrence was born here

forbid: any mapping justified by basename alone
ended for occ-a1 - the file is still there and no site removal was observed
new for occ-b1 - no added path and no added site; this is the fabricated birth
no-predecessor-revision as a reason - revision A exists and is right there
